newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News - Nov 26.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News - Nov 26.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

The Australian economy remains on track for solid investment-led growth this financial year, with companies sharply increasing their planned capital spending for the rest of 1996/97, according to the latest Australian Bureau of Statistics survey of private capital expenditure. Federal Treasurer Peter Costello said the figures supported the budget's prediction of a 14 percent year-on-year rise in investment, but warned the recent surge by the Australian dollar and other pressures could restrain investment in some sectors. Page 1.

Optus Communications chief executive Ziggy Switkowski yesterday warned the federal government that its move to force broadband cables underground would increase the cost of cable rollout by three to six times and Optus would take legal action if changes to the Telecommunications Code have "commercial consequences". Page 2.

Macquarie Bank MBL.AX indicated yesterday it would assume a key role in three different consortia pursuing the Commonwealth's rail assets, including a partnership with Howard Smith's rail engineering arm, A. Goninan and Co, and former National Rail operations maager Mike Purcell in the Great Southern Railway Ltd, which will tender for all of Australian National except the passenger services. Page 5.

To reopen the way for the A$4 billion sharemarket listing of Optus Communications, Optus and the Seven Network Ltd have begun peace negotiations aimed at settling their legal dispute. Seven is pushing for Kerry Packer's Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd to reduce its involvement in Optus Vision, a scenario that will be helped by the departure of Optus chief executive Geoff Cousins, a director of PBL. Page 23.

A Korean consortium, led by Hyundai Corporation, The Halla Group and Tong Yang Global Corporation, has offered to take up to 15 percent of Anaconda Nickel NL's A$900 million Murrin Murrin deposit in Western Australian for A$105 million. Page 25.

Sydney Harbour Casino Ltd chief Neil Gamble has indicated improved relations with the New South Wales Government will be a priority in his new role. The casino has been unsuccessfully campaigning for a lower tax rate on high roller gamblers to allow it to compete with interstate competitors, who have a 10 percent rate, compared with Sydney's 45. Page 25.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Data prepared by federal government officials for the government's review of industry assistance reveals the inquiry will look at 132 business programmes in a sweeping audit of A$2.3 billion in taxpayer subsidies to manufacturers, farmers, miners and the sevices sector this financial year. Page 21.

Japanese metals giants Furukawa Co Ltd and Nissho Iwai Corp have acquired RTZ-CRA's defunct Southern Copper smelter at Port Kembla and are proposing a A$250 million overhaul of the plant as part of a plan to lift annual output from 80,000 tonnes to 120,000 tonnes. Page 21.

Following the release of Bureau of Statistics data indicating new capital expenditure has risen 0.9 percent in the September quarter, on top of a total gain of 21.1 percent in the previous two quarters, hopes for another cut in official interest rates cooled significantly. Page 21.

As a new wave of takeover speculation swept the market yesterday ahead of this week's interim report from the Wallis inquiry into the financial system, speculative buying in major banks and regional lender Bank of Melbourne Ltd pushed the banking index higher. Page 21.

Following the announcement earlier this month that Swiss commodities house Glencore International AG was willing to pay A$350 million to secure 30 to 49 percent of Anaconda Nickel NL's Murrin Murrin nickel project in Western Australia, a Korean consortium has expressed interest in acquiring a 15 percent stake at a cost of A$105 million. Page 23.

The Association of Mining and Exploration Companies, the mining industry lobby group, has joined a long list of politicians and industry groups in attacking the federal government's decision to remove the income tax exemption from the sale of tenements by bona fide prospectors. Page 23.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Economists were surprised yesterday by the release of the strongest quarterly business investment survey in eight years. The figures showed total expenditure rose by 0.9 percent in the September quarter, taking annual capex spending growth to 25.3 percent over the year - the strongest indication in months that the economy would emerge from the doldrums. Page 29.

Sydney Harbour Casino chief executive Neil Gamble, who was appointed to the position five weeks ago, is preparing for phase two, which will concentrate on a mixture of marketing, leadership and government lobbying in an effort to get a lower rate of tax for the profitable offshore high-rollers market. Page 29.

Optus Vision is expected to make an announcement this week on who will replace Geoff Cousins as chief executive after Cousins, who recently brokered the A$120 million rescue package of the Australian Rugby league competition, announced on Friday that he would be quitting the pay-TV group and would not be taking up the role of chairman due to a serious illness in his family. Page 29.

An Australian Securities Commission spokeswoman has revealed the ASC has made no formal recommendations to the Director of Public Prosecutions about Solomon Lew's role in the Yannon affair, which cost Coles Myer A$18 million, despite having admitted he had participated in the deal. Page 29.

Optus Communications chief executive Ziggy Switkowski said yesterday Optus could not adhere to federal government plans to toughen the code of conduct for cable rollout - a plan which would see carriers forced to place cables underground unless local councils agree to overhead lines - due to the cost involved. Page 31.

Following Kerry Packer's Consolidated Press Holdings' decision in September to reduce its shareholding in the Melbourne-based Crown Ltd, Lloyd Williams' construction company Hudson Conway has quit its investment in Packer's Publishing and Broadcasting in a deal thought to be worth A$41 million. Page 31.
THE AGE

Following the Federal Government's decision last week to force communications carriers to negotiate with local governments on the issue of overhead cabling, Optus chief executive Ziggy Switkowski told a Melbourne luncheon yesterday that the underground opion was unthinkable and made the business unviable. Page C1.

Despite the Australian Securities Commission claiming that Coles Myer's major shareholder Solomon Lew "was aware of all aspects "of the Yannon affair and had participated in it, an ASC spokesperson said the ASC had made no formal recommendations to the director of public prosecutions and the defences the commission was raising in the Federal Court case had no implications for a decision on the Yannon investigation. Page C1.

After two blocks of more than seven million Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd shares each changed hands after the market closed on Friday, speculation increased yesterday that Lloyd Williams' property group Hudson Conway had sold its A$40 million stake in Kerry Packer's group. Page C1.

In a move which will give Forrestania Gold NL full ownership of the West Australian Bounty mine, Forrestania had called on Canadian-based LionOre Mining International to help it acquire Normandy Mining's 63 percent interest in the mine for about A$40 million. Bounty is forecast to produce 115,000 ounces of gold in 1996/97, up from 88,633 ounces last year. Page C2.

Alkane Exploration NL announced yesterday that drilling near the south end of the Proprietary zone at its Peak Hill operation in New South Wales had returned a 60.4-metre intersection from 132.6-193 metres, grading 3.68 grams of old a tonne and 0.31 percent copper. Page C2.

Australian Chamber of Manufactures executive director Allan Handberg and other industry leaders have congratulated the federal government on its settlement of the Howe Leather dispute with the U.S, which had put A$3 billion of exports at risk, but they said the company must be given fair compensation. Page C3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 373-1800
